report_meta.title: Packing Time & Motion Study — LV vs HV Comparison
report_meta.subtitle: Week 24 Baseline vs Halfway Day Sale
report_meta.period_label: Week 24 (8–14 Jun) vs Halfway Day Sale (25 Jun–1 Jul) 2026

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.text: Under roughly 2x the order volume of the Low Volume baseline, banner-wide pack execution held up: the true High Volume average (5.7 min, excluding Cornubia's genuine bulk-order outlier) is close to the 6.95-minute Low Volume banner average, and several stores got faster under load, not slower. The real story is dispersion, not a banner-wide decline -- Carnival improved by almost 13 minutes while Cornubia and Bloemfontein each got dramatically slower, for different and specific reasons at each site.

sections.title: Banner Average Pack Time — LV Baseline vs HV (Halfway Day Sale)

executive_facts.statement: The true banner average pack time under Sale volume (5.7 min, excluding Cornubia's bulk-order outlier) is barely above the 6.95-minute Low Volume baseline -- packing execution scaled with volume better than the headline HV KPI (7.9 min) suggests.
Carnival's almost 13-minute improvement suggests whatever changed there -- staffing, layout, or process -- is worth checking as a repeatable practice for the slower stores, not just a one-off result.

Cornubia went from the fastest store in the Low Volume baseline to the slowest in absolute terms under Sale volume -- but this is order-mix driven (genuine large Sale orders), not a process regression, and should not be read alongside the other deltas as if it were comparable.

Bloemfontein and Woodmead both got materially slower under volume, and both changes are attached to thin or partial samples in at least one period -- these deltas are directionally useful but should not be treated with the same confidence as stores with full samples in both periods.

Aggregate dwell risk is not directly comparable across periods with the data supplied: the Low Volume figure reported is a WARNING-band rate, while the High Volume figure available is a CRITICAL-band rate -- a stricter, higher-severity threshold. These use different severity definitions, and the missing LV critical-only rate should be sourced before treating them as equivalent.

sections.text: This is not a banner-wide 'volume broke the process' story but 11 individual store stories -- the two largest movements (Cornubia, up; Carnival, down) both have specific, identified causes and neither should be allowed to set the narrative for the other nine stores.

sections.title: Pack Time Change, LV to HV — Stores With Data in Both Periods (worst regression to best improvement)

rankings.scope_label: Change in average pack time, minutes (positive = slower under volume)

executive_facts.statement: Amanzimtoti and Springfield both got faster under Sale volume (-1.20 and -0.53 min respectively) -- consistent with the separate High Volume finding that both stores' real constraint is trolley dwell, not pack speed, so packers had no reason to slow down.

Gqeberha's apparent 4.6-minute improvement should be treated with real caution -- both its LV and HV samples were affected by data-quality issues (LV bulk outlier exclusion, HV contamination strip leaving only 3 genuine observations), so this delta may reflect sample composition as much as a genuine process change.

Cape Gate, Crown Mines and Alberton all improved by roughly two minutes each under volume, a consistent enough pattern across three unrelated stores to suggest a genuine banner-level readiness improvement between the two study periods, not three isolated coincidences.

sections.title: Stores With HV Pack Data, No LV Pack Data
sections.text:
• Silverlakes — First-ever submission for this store; observation dates fall outside the stated Sale window -- see data quality flags.
  • Strubens Valley — LV had dwell data only, no pack observations.
  • Riversands — LV had dwell data only, no pack observations.
  • Montague Gardens — LV had dwell data only, no pack observations.
  • Germiston — LV file was submitted blank; this is the first real pack-time data for this store.

executive_facts.statement: Four stores with Low Volume pack data submitted nothing usable for the High Volume period (Ottery, Pietermaritzburg, Vaal, Mbombela) -- this is a bigger visibility gap during the period that matters most operationally, and closing it should outrank most other follow-up items.

Three stores (Strubens Valley, Riversands, Montague Gardens) had dwell data but no pack observations in the Low Volume period, and only gained pack-time visibility in the High Volume study -- their HV figures are a first baseline, not a trend, and should not be described as an improvement or decline until a second data point exists.

sections.title: Data Quality & Comparability Flags
sections.text:
• LV figures not independently re-verified this session — the Low Volume figures used in this comparison come from the project's own stated 'key verified figures' rather than a raw LV workbook supplied and re-checked in this analysis. The High Volume figures were independently cross-checked against the source management report and consolidated workbook.
  • Dwell severity bands are not directly comparable — the only aggregate LV dwell statistic available is a WARNING-band rate; the only aggregate HV figure available is a CRITICAL-band rate, a stricter, higher-severity threshold. A true apples-to-apples comparison requires the LV critical-only rate, which was not supplied.
  • Cornubia and Woodmead deltas are not process signals — Cornubia's increase is bulk order-mix driven; Woodmead's LV baseline was a partial 5-observation submission. Both are included for completeness but should not be read as packer performance changes.
  • Silverlakes has no LV baseline at all — it is a first-time HV submission with an unresolved observation-date anomaly (see the High Volume data quality note); its figures should not be treated as a stable comparison point yet.

Before this comparison is used in a management deck: source the missing LV critical-band dwell rate so the dwell comparison can be made honestly, and treat the Cornubia and Gqeberha deltas as annotated exceptions rather than banner-representative figures.

provenance.extraction_notes: LV figures are taken from the project's own stated 'key verified figures' in the supplied context brief, not from a raw LV workbook uploaded and independently checked in this session -- flagged throughout as a lower-confidence source than the HV figures, which were cross-checked against the actual HV docx/xlsx. Only stores with real pack-time observations in both periods are shown as deltas; stores with data in only one period are listed separately rather than assigned a fabricated 0 or blank delta. The LV dwell WARNING rate (38%) and HV dwell CRITICAL rate (37.5%) use different severity thresholds and are not blended into a single comparable figure.
